summary: Two changes are worth reviewing in this fictional project. First, remove a permission that allows every shell command without asking. Then shorten the project instructions to make them easier to maintain. No configuration changes have been made.

coverage.summary: Reviewed the project’s permission settings, instruction file and 10 recorded sessions.
limitations: Two sessions were outside the scan limit, so the usage figures describe only the 10 sessions reviewed.

context_baseline_median.label: Typical context at session start
context_baseline_median.explanation: Half the reviewed sessions started with at least this much context already loaded. This includes more than the project instruction file; it does not tell us how much a single edit would save.
context_baseline_median.source: First responses in 10 fictional session transcripts

instruction_tokens.label: Size of project instructions
instruction_tokens.explanation: Approximate size of CLAUDE.md, calculated from its character count. This is not a measured bill or a promised saving.

findings.title: Every shell command is pre-approved
findings.why: A blanket permission removes an approval checkpoint for shell commands. A mistaken command could change or delete files without pausing for your review.
findings.evidence: The project settings contain the allow rule Bash(*), which covers every shell command.

fix.summary: Remove the blanket rule. Approve specific routine commands as they are needed.

findings.effort: 5 minutes, including checking the resulting settings

findings.title: The instruction file repeats the same setup steps
findings.why: Repeated instructions make the file harder to maintain. Updating one copy can leave another copy out of date.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md repeats the same installation and test commands in three sections. Its total length is 7,200 characters.

fix.summary: Keep one setup section and remove the duplicate steps after checking that no unique guidance is lost.
steps: Check that the documented setup and test commands still work.

caveats: This quick audit did not compare settings with current online documentation.
The report does not establish whether organization-managed policy overrides these project settings.
